meta.method: Close-up photography of the physical board for connector inventory, plus commands run on the running board over serial and SSH for everything software-visible. No vendor schematic was available. Elk's desktop-devkit README was available and is cited where it is the source.
meta.caveat: Silkscreen labels were read from photographs. Where a label was partially obscured it is marked. This file describes ONE board; jumper positions are per-unit and yours may differ.

verified.definition: Passed real signal or ran a command that proved this, on hardware, in this project.

probed.definition: Software on the board reported it (dmesg, lsusb, sysfs); the thing itself was never exercised.

silkscreen.definition: Read from board photographs; the connector is visibly fitted but unused.

documented.definition: Stated in a config file or vendor doc we relied on, not independently confirmed.

inferred.definition: Reasoned from other facts. Treat as a hypothesis.

meta.entry_level_referent: A port's top-level `verification` grades the CONNECTOR - that it exists and is what its label says. It never grades the jack-to-channel binding.
meta.inheritance: A nested block without `verification` inherits its parent's; where it carries one, that wins.
meta.null_means: not determined by this audit - never 'none'

corrections.claim: The Stomp has no MIDI jacks.
corrections.correction: The board has MIDI IN and MIDI OUT on 3.5 mm TRS.
corrections.source_of_error: Taken from the product-page I/O summary and repeated for a week.

soc.simd: NEON, VFPv3, VFPv4 (single-precision only, no double-precision lanes)

som.evidence: Board photograph of the SoM module

memory.evidence: free -m on the board. ram_mb is the nominal DRAM capacity; free -m reports less because of kernel reservation.

storage.note: mmcblk1 with boot0/boot1 partitions, which only eMMC has. Root partition ships ~83% full with under 200 MB free, and /home/mind lives on it. /udata is a separate ~1.9 GB partition with ~1.8 GB free - put large files there.

rtc.impact: The board's wall clock is wrong, so file mtimes on this board are meaningless. Identify deployed artefacts by sha256, never by timestamp.
rtc.evidence: `date` on the board returned a 2025 date while the host clock read 2026.
rtc.present_evidence: Never probed. `ls /dev/rtc*`, `hwclock -r` and `dmesg | grep rtc` were all never run. The STM32MP157 carries an on-chip RTC peripheral and this board has a VBAT "battery / backup rail" header, so "no RTC" is a hypothesis, not a finding. A wrong clock is equally consistent with an RTC present but unset, a dead backup cell, or no NTP.

gotchas.evidence: BusyBox flag and applet failures hit directly during serial-console work; systemd-logind reaping observed when SSH sessions dropped background processes.
items: BusyBox has no `base64` binary; use python3 to decode file transfers
systemd-logind reaps user processes on logout; the serial console login persists where SSH does not. If the reaped process is Sushi, see `lifecycle` - that reap delivers a fatal signal.

disputed_gotchas.evidence: Recorded as observed during the 2026-08-26 serial session ("`ip` absent - use `ifconfig`"), but CONTRADICTED by three documents in the sibling repo which prescribe `ip addr` on the board (docs/ELK-COMMANDS.md:147, docs/PROFILING.md:15, stomp/PORT.md:40). Those three are laptop-written prescriptions, not recorded observations, so they are the weaker source - but `command -v ip` was never run and one side is wrong. Do not rely on either until it is settled. See open_questions.ip_binary_present.
items: `ip` may be absent (use `ifconfig`) - DISPUTED, see evidence

sushi.evidence: Read from Sushi's own gRPC SystemController.GetBuildInfo (info.version) by the profiling harness on the board - recorded per row in data/profiling-results.csv, 45 board rows, all 1.3.0. Do NOT try to read it from /usr/bin/sushi, which is a wrapper shell script.
gotchas: Sushi has NO xrun counter. `max >= 1.0` in its timing statistics is the only dropout signal, and nothing will tell you to look.

Sushi launched as a systemd USER unit gets ZERO audio callbacks on this image, and nothing says so. The user manager (started by logind) runs at rtprio 0 / memlock 8 MB and a unit cannot exceed its manager, so LimitRTPRIO=99 on the unit is silently capped to 0. RASPA then opens audio_evl, exchanges nothing (dmesg: `ping=0 pong=0`, `dev closed`) and the engine reports avg=max=0.000 while every gRPC write returns SUCCESS and never applies. An ssh login shell has rtprio 99 / memlock unlimited from pam; launch Sushi from one (setsid nohup, as tools/sushi_board.sh does). Verified 2026-09-02: /proc/<pid>/limits under the unit = 0/8 MB, from the shell = 99/unlimited, and only the latter logs `AUDIO_PROC_START cpu_num: 1`. `loginctl enable-linger mind` (root) is now set so shell-launched daemons survive logout; it does not fix the unit cap.
/usr/bin/sushi is a wrapper shell script that selects sushi_b32/b64/b128. `ldd` and `strings` on it tell you nothing - inspect sushi_b<size> instead.

audio_engine.evidence: dmesg audio_evl channel enumeration; AUDIO_PROC_START cpu_num: 1
audio_engine.timing_unit: Sushi's Timings {average, min, max} are a FRACTION of the block period, NOT milliseconds - elkpy's docstring says ms and is wrong. 1.0 = deadline_ms (1.333). Every unitless timing number in this file is in these units.
audio_engine.timing_unit_evidence: RUNBOOK.md section 0; tools/profile_sweep.py header. The CSV's thiri_max_ms column is DERIVED from thiri_max by the harness, so it corroborates nothing on its own.
audio_engine.critical_note: CPU 0 is idle. Any companion process (hardware daemon, control app) left unpinned lands on CPU 1 and fights the audio callback. Pinning A/B, one paired session on the live rig config (60 s steady playback per arm), as a fraction of the block period: worst block 0.770 alone, 2.273 with an unpinned control surface, 0.760 with `taskset -c 0`. The AVERAGE never moved (~0.60) in any of the three. 0.770 is that session's control arm, NOT the board's general clean baseline: across the unloaded board rows in data/profiling-results.csv the worst block ranges roughly 0.74-0.83 at the same ~0.60 average. Budget headroom against 0.83; read a pinning regression only from a multiple-of-baseline jump like 2.273, not from 0.83 variance.
audio_engine.critical_note_evidence: Measured on this board in this project; conditions and results recorded at the rig runner in this project's private plugin repo. NOT in data/profiling-results.csv - no row in that dataset varies thread affinity (affinity_psr is "na" in all 51 rows) and tools/ has no harness that pins or unpins a companion process.

buffer_size_selection.evidence: The three binaries and the wrapper were read on the board, and the running block size read back per profiling row via Sushi's GetBuildInfo. No size other than 64 was ever selected, so the selector's effect is unexercised.

channel_names_as_reported.caveat: The driver's own channel_name strings. Channels 1-3 are all reported as "-R", which looks like a driver naming quirk rather than four right channels. Do not read meaning into the names beyond channel 0.
channel_names_as_reported.evidence: dmesg audio_evl: Input/Output channel N info, channel_name field

practice.evidence: Every stop path in this project sends SIGINT and only SIGINT (tools/sushi_board.sh stop -> `kill -INT`; the rig runner in this project's private plugin repo). This proves the procedure works, not what the other signals do.

failure_mode.effect: SIGTERM or SIGKILL wedges the audio_evl driver. The next Sushi launch hangs and the board must be power-cycled.
failure_mode.evidence: Stated as known Elk driver behaviour in the sibling repo's bug report and port notes, and in RUNBOOK.md. We NEVER deliberately reproduced it - the rule was followed, never tested.

traps: Elk's `run-example.sh` traps INT only, and its trap runs `kill 0` - SIGTERM to the whole process group. Signal it with `kill -INT $(pgrep -f run-example.sh)`.
A dropped SSH session can deliver the fatal signal: systemd-logind reaps the user scope on logout. Start with `setsid nohup`, or from the serial console.
/tmp/sushi.log flushes only on a clean exit. An empty log after a kill means nothing, not 'no errors'. Use --log-flush-interval=1.

ports.label: 9V
ports.evidence: The board was powered and run from a 9V centre-negative pedal supply throughout this project. The centre-negative symbol was read from the silkscreen, not measured. The >=1.5 A minimum and "not USB-powered" are documented only in the sibling repo's port notes and spec - current draw was never measured and running the board on USB alone was never attempted. (Those two sources differ: ">=1.5 A" against "1.5A".)

ports.label: GUITAR IN L
ports.evidence: Elk's desktop-devkit README (README.md:199) enumerates the Stomp's four engine channels as "inputs = guitar inputs L&R and stereo line in, outputs: guitar outputs L&R and stereo headphones out"; guitar in L is first, hence channel 0. Separately, the board configs that declare an input at all use {engine_channel: 0, track_channel: 0}; the rest declare "inputs": [] and generate audio internally, including the configs behind every board row in data/profiling-results.csv. We never passed signal into this jack with the other inputs silent, so the jack-to-channel binding WAS documented. VERIFIED 2026-09-02 (tools/iotest.py in): a Roland Aerophone AE-10's 1/4" output played into GUITAR IN L appeared on engine channel 0 at peak -6.5 dBFS (rms -22.3, crest 15.8 dB) while channels 1/2/3 stayed at the noise floor -- so the binding is isolated and measured. The level is healthy, NOT the ~15x-hot figure from the internal-bus gain-staging note; that was a different point in the chain, not this jack.

ports.label: GUITAR IN R
ports.evidence: Connector fitted and labelled on the board. Never used. Channel 1 is an assumption of symmetry with L, corroborated by the devkit README's ordering.

ports.label: LINE IN
ports.evidence: Connector fitted and labelled, distinct from GUITAR IN. Never used. The channel mapping comes from Elk's desktop-devkit README:199, which lists the four engine INPUTS as guitar in L&R plus stereo line in - so line in is 2/3. No signal was ever passed into this jack, and the routing jumpers are per-unit, so this is documented, not measured.
ports.note: A separate physical jack from GUITAR IN - not a level switch on the same jack. Jumper block not identified; see open_questions.jumper_matrix.

ports.label: SPDIF_RX
ports.evidence: Silkscreen only. Digital audio input. Never investigated.

ports.label: GUITAR OUT L
ports.evidence: Connector fitted and labelled. Never monitored from this jack, so the positive binding still rests on Elk's devkit README:199 (four engine outputs = guitar out L&R plus stereo headphones). What IS measured (2026-09-02, tools/iotest.py out 0): engine channel 0 driven alone is SILENT at HEADPHONE OUT and LINE OUT, which both carry 2/3 -- so 0/1 is a distinct pair from 2/3, and this jack is the only remaining place for it. Patch it and run `out 0` / `out 1` to raise this to verified.

ports.label: GUITAR OUT R
ports.evidence: As GUITAR OUT L: binding from devkit README:199, connector read from photographs, never monitored. The 0/1-vs-2/3 pair distinction is measured (channel 0 alone is silent at the 2/3 jacks); channel 1 alone not yet run.

ports.label: LINE OUT
ports.evidence: 2026-09-02, tools/iotest.py on the board: with ONLY engine channel 2 driven (chura123 loop, unity) audio was heard at LINE OUT and at HEADPHONE OUT and nowhere else patched; then with ONLY channel 3 driven (880 Hz sine) the same two jacks. LINE OUT therefore carries the same 2/3 pair as the headphone jack in this unit's jumper state -- it is NOT a fifth channel and NOT exclusive with the headphones.
ports.note: Which jumper puts it there was still not determined (both jacks were live at once, so the shunts were not moved). Left/right within the pair was not attributed either: the listener reported "both jacks" for each channel, not which side.

ports.label: HEADPHONE OUT
ports.evidence: 2026-09-02, tools/iotest.py: engine channel 2 driven ALONE (chura123 loop) was heard here; then channel 3 driven ALONE (880 Hz) was heard here. Each channel isolated in turn, so the 2/3 binding is measured, not taken from the devkit README. (Earlier evidence had driven 0,1,2,3 together and could not attribute anything.) Left/right within the pair not attributed.

ports.label: MIDI IN
ports.evidence: Connector fitted and labelled on the board, beside the Elk logo. Never used.
ports.note: No ALSA MIDI device was ever attributed to this jack. The only MIDI client seen in this board's `aconnect` listing was the USB-attached wind controller, so whether these jacks appear to ALSA at all is unknown, not absent.
ports.warning: TRS MIDI has two incompatible pinouts (Type A and Type B). Which this is has NOT been established. Check before wiring anything to it.

ports.label: MIDI OUT
ports.evidence: Connector fitted and labelled. Never used.
ports.note: As MIDI IN: no ALSA MIDI device was ever attributed to this jack.
ports.software_blocker: Even with the jack working, Sushi's `midi.track_out_connections` is not declared in its midi_schema.json and validates only because the schema omits `additionalProperties: false`. Too fragile to build on.
ports.software_blocker_evidence: Sibling repo's MIDI-FX notes, from reading Sushi's schema. Never exercised.
ports.warning: Same TRS pinout caveat as MIDI IN.

ports.label: USB TO UART
ports.controller_evidence: The part number appears in this project's notes but no lsusb, dmesg or system_profiler capture recording it survives, and it was not read off the IC. What IS established is that the host sees four tty devices, which is consistent with a quad-channel FTDI.
ports.evidence: Serial console used throughout the project at 115200 baud
ports.note: The host sees FOUR tty devices. The console is the LOWEST-numbered. The device numbering changes when you move the cable to a different host port.

ports.label: USB HOST

controllers.evidence: A Roland Aerophone AE-10 (0582:01d1) enumerated on this controller at full speed.
Seen in dmesg at boot; never carried a device.

ports.bus_pairing_note: The original record paired controllers with buses positionally and non-monotonically, so which number belongs to which controller is no longer reliable. Both numbers were observed; the pairing was not recorded.
ports.evidence: A Roland Aerophone AE-10 (0582:01d1) enumerated here on the OHCI bus at full speed; snd-usb-audio autoloaded with no configuration and the device appeared as an ALSA sequencer client.
ports.note: Only full-speed enumeration through OHCI was exercised. High-speed operation on this jack is untested.
gotchas: A USB MIDI device enumerating is NOT the same as Sushi seeing it. Sushi does not auto-connect to hardware MIDI inputs: its ALSA sequencer client appears asynchronously and must be joined with `aconnect <src>:0 <sushi>:0`. Without that link the cc_mappings are DEAF - config correct, connections registered, nothing logged, parameters never move.
Running `amidi` on the raw device severs that sequencer link. Re-link after any raw MIDI capture.
Restarting Sushi gives it a new client id and drops all connections. Re-link every launch.

ports.label: USB
ports.evidence: dmesg shows `dwc2 49000000.usb-otg: bound driver g_ether` at boot; networking to a host over a single cable, no dongle required (board 10.66.0.2, host 10.66.0.1).
ports.note: The controller is named `usb-otg` and dwc2 on the STM32MP157 is dual-role, so host mode is not ruled out - it was never attempted, and whether the port sources VBUS is unknown. Read `device/gadget` as "gadget is what we proved", not "host is impossible".
gotchas: A charge-only USB-C cable is indistinguishable from a dead board. Check /sys/class/udc/*/state - `not attached` means no host is seen.

ports.label: SD CARD
ports.evidence: mmc0 host controller is present in /sys/class/mmc_host with 0 devices attached. No card was ever inserted.

routing.summary: The audio engine exposes 4 in / 4 out but the board has seven audio jacks - three in (guitar L/R, line in) and four out (guitar L/R, line out, headphones). The output side cannot all be live at once. Which physical jack reaches which codec channel is set by JUMPER POSITION, in hardware, not by software.
routing.practical_rule: If a jack seems dead, check the jumpers before you check your code.
routing.evidence: Jumper blocks are labelled with per-jack names on the silkscreen. The mapping from jumper position to codec channel was NOT determined - we never moved one. This section is a hypothesis about the mechanism, supported by the labelling, not a measured truth table.

jumper_state_as_found.state: not recorded - the shunt positions on this unit were never transcribed
jumper_state_as_found.note: Every observation in this file, including the audio heard at HEADPHONE OUT, was taken with the jumpers exactly as the board shipped; none was moved. A unit whose jumpers sit differently may route differently, and this file gives you no reference state to compare yours against.
jumper_state_as_found.evidence: Basis is routing.evidence ('we never moved one'). The positions themselves were never read off the board or transcribed from the photographs.

blocks.label: PH13
blocks.note: No matching jack silkscreen. Function not determined; PH13/PH14 also read as STM32 port-H pin names, so do not assume this is an audio-jack block.

expansion.evidence: All read from board photographs. Not one was used in this project. The `purpose` strings are the printed label decoded, except where noted.

headers.label: ADC EXP
headers.purpose: analogue inputs beyond the onboard pots
headers.purpose_evidence: The label reads ADC EXP; "beyond the onboard pots" is an interpretation of what such a header would be for, not something the silkscreen states.

headers.label: USART2
headers.purpose: serial, TX/RX/GND on a jumper block

controls.evidence: Enumerated from sensei_config.json, which lists 41 addressable elements. The board's own copy is at /home/mind/sensei_config.json (run_rig.sh invokes `sensei -f` on it); the copy readable off-board is the devkit's board-gui mock, and the two agree on all 41 ids and names. Connector presence was cross-checked against board photographs. This is a declaration of what Sensei exposes, not a measurement: no element's physical actuation was recorded on this board. Real Sensei plus the Guru glue did run on the board during the CPU-pinning sweeps, which proves the daemon loads this map - not that every element responds.
controls.addressing_note: INPUTS are bound by `controller_name` (a name Sensei does not know raises ValueError at register time, listing the available names). OUTPUTS (LEDs, RGB channels) are addressed by numeric id via UpdateLed(controller_id=...).

switches.warning: The silkscreen legend and the Sensei name DIVERGE here. The board is printed KEY 1-4; Sensei calls them SW1-SW4. Guru resolves by name, so controller_name="KEY1" is wrong. For pots and encoders the legend and the name happen to resemble each other - do not generalise that.

preset_switch.reads_as: analog_input on an 8-bit ADC. It arrives as a LEVEL, not a toggle - threshold the analog value into positions.
preset_switch.evidence: sensei_config.json id 37, name PRESET_SW, sensor_type analog_input. Silkscreen label read from board photographs. NEVER EXERCISED - the number of distinct levels and where they sit in 0-255 are unconfirmed.
preset_switch.identification_note: That PRESET_SW is the 4-position rotary is an inference: it is the only one of the 41 entries not otherwise accounted for (1-12 RGB, 13-16 LED, 17-20 SW, 21-28 POT, 29-32 ENC*S, 33-36 ENC, 38-41 DET), and an 8-bit ADC on one pin is the standard way to read a multi-position rotary.

oled.evidence: Pin labels read from the OLED daughterboard in photographs. Driven in this project only via Guru's DisplayManager, never addressed directly.

jack_detect.note: Four controller ids suggesting the board can tell when a cable is inserted in each guitar jack - free auto-switching or mute-on-unplug if it works.
jack_detect.evidence: Four controller ids named GUIT_*_DET in the board's sensei_config.json. Never mapped in the glue app, never handled, and no insertion event was ever observed - so that the detect lines work, and that Sensei emits events for them, is unconfirmed.

banking.mechanism: Elk's Guru glue library indexes its mapping table by mode - MAPPINGS is a list OF lists, with ModeSwitch and CycleMode events already wired to the observer. Most example code defines one mode and stops there.
banking.evidence: Read from the Guru library source on the board - guru/src/guru/mappings.py (ModeSwitch/CycleMode subscriptions; mappings enumerated per mode). Source read, not behaviour observed. This project shipped a single mode, so an agent planning a multi-bank control surface is designing against unrun code.

open_questions.question: Are MIDI IN/OUT Type A or Type B TRS?
open_questions.why: Determines whether hardware MIDI is usable at all, and with which cables.

open_questions.question: Do the hardware MIDI jacks appear to ALSA on this board at all, and does Sushi see them as a MIDI device?
open_questions.why: Bundled with the pinout question this could never close - answering the cheap half leaves the jacks unusable.

open_questions.question: Which jumper position routes which jack to which codec channel? OUTPUT side partly settled 2026-09-02 in this unit's jumper state: engine 2/3 reaches HEADPHONE OUT and LINE OUT (both, each channel isolated), and engine 0 reaches neither -- so the outputs are two distinct pairs. Still open: which shunt does that, the L/R side within each pair, and the whole INPUT side.
open_questions.why: Seven jacks, four channels. Without this, jack selection is guesswork.

open_questions.question: Can the USB-C gadget port act as a USB host, and does it source VBUS?
open_questions.why: The controller is dual-role. If it can host, the board gains a second USB input without a hub.

open_questions.question: What jumper positions was this unit shipped with?

What channel does LINE IN map to? (LINE OUT is settled 2026-09-02: it carries the 2/3 pair together with HEADPHONE OUT -- not exclusive with it. Which jumper selects that, and left/right within the pair, remain open.)
The devkit README says line in is engine channels 2 and 3. Confirm on this board by passing signal into LINE IN alone.
How many distinct levels does PRESET_SW produce, and where do they sit in 0-255?
Does the board have `ip` and `install`? Run `command -v ip install base64`.
open_questions.why: This project's own records contradict each other; one side is wrong and it was never re-checked.

open_questions.question: All timing measurements were taken at 800 MHz. What happens at 400?
Does setting AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE to 32 or 128 actually switch binaries, and what does it do to the headroom numbers?
open_questions.why: Every timing figure in this project was taken at 64 frames / 1.333 ms.

open_questions.question: Does a high-speed device enumerate on the EHCI controller at USB HOST?
Do the GUIT_*_DET lines actually fire, and does Sensei emit events for them?
Is there an RTC? Run `ls /dev/rtc*`, `hwclock -r`, `dmesg | grep -i rtc`.
Does a card mount, and does the SD CARD JUMPER need setting?
